t: In the case of the authorization contained in the table in section 2101(b) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (division B of Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 2629) for Camp Arifjan, Kuwait, for construction of APS Warehouses, the Secretary of the Army may construct up to 74,976 square meters of hardstand parking, 22,741 square meters of access roads, a 6 megawatt power plant, and 50,724 square meters of humidity-controlled warehouses.

fable.w: This section only modifies the scope of a previously authorized military construction project at Camp Arifjan, Kuwait, by specifying what the Secretary of the Army may build. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to object or sue, and there is no rulemaking, comment period, or advisory body. The word "may" could tempt a reading of discretionary process, but it is simply a construction authorization for a federal official.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Army may construct up to 74,976 square meters of hardstand parking, 22,741 square meters of access roads, a 6 megawatt power plant, and 50,724 square meters of humidity-controlled warehouses.

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes a federal official (the Secretary of the Army) to carry out specific construction projects. It does not require or recommend consultation with any outside parties, such as the public, state governments, or advisory boards. The decision-making process described is entirely internal to the federal government.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of the Army may construct up to 74,976 square meters of hardstand parking, 22,741 square meters of access roads, a 6 megawatt power plant, and 50,724 square meters of humidity-controlled warehouses.

opus.w: This section only changes the scope of a military construction project at Camp Arifjan, Kuwait, setting how much parking, road, power plant and warehouse space the Secretary of the Army may build. No party outside the federal government is involved in the decision, and the section has no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. The Secretary's discretionary 'may' is construction authority, not rulemaking authority, so it does not count as participation.

It does not require or recommend consultation with any outside parties, such as state governments, the public, or advisory committees. The decision-making authority rests entirely within the federal executive branch.
